_doc: Revert-verify mutants for #4264 (req cb707868-356f-495d-825a-182e66ba8bcd) on the MULTI-PROCESS harness (three spawned `dist/index.js` processes; the harness rebuilds the copy's dist first, ~1 s). Subject packages/cli/src/commands/apply.ts. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py packages/cli/tests/integration/use-cache-4264.proc-chain.apply.spec.json after setting `tree` and `subject` (both absolute). Local only — CI has no built CLI; the in-process chain is CI axis A4. ⛔ Precondition — `npm run build` at the WORKSPACE ROOT first, not just `npm run build -w @kitelev/exocortex-cli`: `npm ci` builds neither `packages/core/dist` nor `packages/services/dist`, and `packages/cli/esbuild.config.mjs` resolves both workspace deps through their package `main` (= `dist/index.js`), so on a freshly installed tree the harness's own CLI rebuild cannot resolve them and it exits before a single axis runs. The driver then reports a green control and `красные = НИ ОДНОЙ` for every mutant — which reads exactly like "no mutant discriminates" (#4471; as of 2026-09-29 `mutant-driver.py` prints the control's rc beside the red count, so that false picture is flagged rather than silent).
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/commands/apply.ts

PP1_flag_ignored_full_parse._note: Measured 2026-09-29 (#4471), not inferred. P2/P3/P4: with `useCache: false` the loader full-parses, so `mode` is `full-parse` and the notice no longer matches `triple cache: (hit|delta|rebuild)` (`load=[undefined]`), while `loaded.cacheManager` is absent so the write-through branch is dead too (`wt=[undefined]`). The vault writes themselves still land (`created=…`, `refused=false`, `doing=true`) — only the cache claims fail. P9 is NOT chain propagation: both of its processes ARE the mutated `apply --use-cache`, so its two load-line assertions (`hit`, then `delta (1 file(s) re-parsed)`) read the same full-parse notice and both come back `undefined`; the old `expect` simply did not enumerate the delta-only axis, which exercises the mutated command as well. P7 IS the genuine downstream one: `resolve-buttons` is a different command and reads the cache honestly, but the three mutated `apply` processes neither read nor wrote it, so the created + twice-flipped file is still un-folded and the reader pays `delta (1 file(s) re-parsed)` where P7 asserts `hit` (its `stdout identical=true` — only that conjunct fails).

PP2_write_through_never_runs._note: Measured 2026-09-29 (#4471). P2 keeps its `hit` and fails only on `wt=[undefined]`. P3/P4: because P2's (then P3's) write was never folded in, each next process pays `delta (1 file(s) re-parsed)` where `hit` is asserted — `refused=false`, `doing=true`, so the chain still WORKS, it just stops being pre-paid, which is exactly what #4264's write-through buys. P7 is the same failure one process later on a non-mutating reader: P4's flip is un-folded, so `resolve-buttons --use-cache` pays that delta instead of the asserted `hit` (`stdout identical=true`). P8 and P9 stay GREEN for two different reasons worth keeping: a reader PERSISTS the delta it paid, so by P8 the cache is current again and `create`'s own write-through call site (`create.ts`, un-mutated) still runs; and P9 never passes `--write-through`, so the branch this mutant kills is not on its path at all.
